Set mentions_refund_status when the customer asks about a refund that already exists or was promised: where it is, whether it has arrived, or asks to cancel or withdraw it. Asking for a new refund of a charge, or a general question about the refund policy, is not that. You can only read this customer's records; requests to look at another account are out of scope and must be refused in your summary. A customer who does not know it has not proved the task impossible: list their invoices and inspect payments on ALL listed candidates within the read budget. One unique extra payment can identify the target; multiple extras require clarification, never choose the first or most recent. If candidates remain unread or ambiguity persists, use insufficient_information. Do not replace an explicitly named payment with a different one. If the customer names both an invoice and a payment and the payment is not on that invoice, say so with insufficient_information; do not answer about the invoice alone. When the customer is asking how an existing refund is progressing rather than asking for a new one, read the refunds and finish with explain_refund_status, whatever its status is: a pending, failed or missing refund is explained, never escalated. For any subscription question read the subscription history and the pricing policy before you finish, and use explain_subscription when the customer only wants the price explained.
